name: A-level Accounting (AQA 7127)
material_vintage: AQA A-level Accounting (7127) specification, Version 1.0 (22 December 2016, for teaching from September 2017 onwards), the current version linked from aqa.org.uk/7127, itemised on 2026-09-27: all 18 subject content sections (3.1-3.18) at this course's own deepest sub-lettering, and the nine quantitative skills in the annex (QS1-QS9). Assessment: two 3-hour written papers, 120 marks each (50% each, 240 marks total). Paper 1 (Financial Accounting) assesses sections 1-8 and 14-18; Paper 2 (Accounting for Analysis and Decision-Making) assesses sections 1-3, 8-13 and 17-18. Each paper has three compulsory sections: Section A (30 marks: 10 multiple-choice questions plus short-answer questions), Section B (40 marks: structured questions), Section C (50 marks: two 25-mark extended-response questions, each split 5 AO2/20 AO3 marks and marked by a five-level response scheme). Overall AO weighting is approximately AO1 24-26%, AO2 33-35%, AO3 40-42%. Stage tests and the mock are original questions in AQA's style; every numerical answer was computed when the course was built.
level_source: RQF Level 3 (GCE A-level), per Ofqual's register listing for AQA 7127

learner_notices.text: This course marks its own stage tests to a 60% pass mark and its mock exam to 50% overall (at least 40% on each paper) as this library's own standard for secure work. AQA sets its actual grade boundaries afresh for each real exam series (they are not fixed at 50%/60%), so treat these as a study target, not a predicted grade.

This library has no GCSE Accounting course, so there is no GCSE-tier prerequisite for this A-level (the same position as A-level Politics). If you have not studied accounting before, expect the early stages (S01-S03) to move quickly through unfamiliar terms - take them slowly.

Real AQA answer booklets use printed pro-forma layouts (ruled statements of profit or loss, T-accounts, control account templates). This course teaches the same structure and labelling in plain text/markdown; practise laying your own answers out clearly under headed subtotals, as a real answer booklet would require.
